learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the amazing biological mechanisms of cloning (asexual) and combining traits (sexual) that allow life to continue on Earth generation after generation.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Reproduction starts with copying the DNA in a cell. This copying is never 100% perfect, which creates variations. These tiny variations are the basis of evolution and survival.

Only one parent is involved. Types include Binary Fission (Amoeba), Budding (Hydra/Yeast), Spore Formation (Rhizopus/Fungus), Regeneration (Planaria), and Vegetative Propagation in plants (growing from stem/roots).

Flowers are the reproductive organs. Pollination transfers pollen from the anther to the stigma. A pollen tube grows to the ovary where Fertilization happens, turning the ovule into a seed and the ovary into a fruit.

Involves two parents producing male (sperm) and female (egg/ovum) gametes. Fertilization happens in the fallopian tube. The embryo attaches to the uterus lining and gets nutrition from the mother via the 'Placenta'.

Sexual contact can transmit diseases (STDs like HIV/AIDS). Contraception prevents unwanted pregnancies using mechanical barriers (condoms), chemical methods (pills), or surgical methods (vasectomy/tubectomy).

fun_activity.title: 🥔 The Potato Clone
fun_activity.instructions: Take an old potato that has small 'eyes' (buds) growing on it. Cut a piece containing an eye and plant it in wet soil. In a few days, a whole new potato plant will grow! This is Vegetative Propagation.

exam_tips: 📌 Draw and practice labeling the parts of a Flower and the Female Reproductive System.
📌 Understand the difference between Self-pollination (same flower) and Cross-pollination (different flower).
📌 A common question is: 'What happens if the egg is not fertilized?' Answer: The thick lining of the uterus breaks down and sheds as blood (Menstruation).
quick_recap: ⭐ Asexual reproduction creates exact copies, while sexual reproduction mixes DNA to create variation.
⭐ The placenta acts as an exchange station for oxygen, nutrients, and waste between mother and fetus.
⭐ The use of condoms is the only contraceptive method that also protects against Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs).
